idiom_name: Codable enum with associated values + switch dispatch (XPC/NSSecureCoding for legacy)
implementation_notes: Since Swift 5.5 the compiler synthesises Codable for enums with associated values (SE-0295), so `enum Command: Codable` is a closed command set, JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder is the codec and an exhaustive `switch` is the invoker - no base class and no registry. The synthesised JSON shape nests associated values under the case name, so case names are the wire contract. Where the far side is another Apple process, NSXPCConnection is the transport, but XPC wants @objc-compatible classes: the command must then be an NSSecureCoding class decoded through an NSKeyedUnarchiver created with requiresSecureCoding and an explicit class allow-list, or the boundary is re-shaped as an enum plus distributed actors.
pitfalls: NSKeyedUnarchiver without requiresSecureCoding (and without setClass(_:forClassName: allow-lists) instantiates arbitrary classes from an archive, so an XPC command payload from an untrusted sender is a code-execution surface - never use unarchiveObject(with:).
The synthesised Codable shape nests associated values under the case name, so renaming a case or adding a label changes the wire format; toolchains before Swift 5.5 need hand-written CodingKeys.

Commands crossing actor boundaries must be Sendable, and distributed actors encode call arguments through an explicit codable contract - a class command with mutable state will not compile into a distributed call.
